To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Toll-like receptor (TLR)-2 ligands, including lipopeptides, are potent inducers of Th2-type responses and are able to exacerbate allergic airway inflammation, whereas TLR-7 and TLR-9 ligands, including imidazoquinoline and phosphorothioate oligonucleotides (CpG-ODN), are strong inducers of Th1 and Th2 type responses and are able of reducing airway inflammation in experimental models of asthma
Toll-like receptor ligands may represent a novel class of drugs to treat allergic disorders, but their efficacy in humans has to be proven.
TLR agonists are promising novel pharmaceuticals for the treatment of allergic diseases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new therapeutic agents for the treatment of asthma, allergy and other inflammatory diseases.
the role of Toll‐like receptors (TLRs) as a novel target in the treatment of allergic disorders and the development of novel therapeutic strategies.
the molecular basis of allergic disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the field of TLR‐based immunotherapies is in its infancy, with only a limited number of TLR ligand‐based immunomodulators currently available for clinical use in the treatment of allergic disorders, but that the future is bright.

, at present, TLR ligands have a great promise for the prevention and treatment of allergic disorders but further research is needed to define optimal doses, routes of administration, and to identify patients who will benefit from these novel therapies.

TLR ligands are a promising new class of immunotherapeutic agents for the prevention or therapy of allergic diseases, but that further studies are required to identify the optimal TLR ligands, the optimal routes of administration, and the appropriate patient populations for these novel therapies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TLRs are a promising target for the development of new immunotherapeutic strategies in allergic diseases.
the TLRs are key regulators in the development of allergic inflammation and that the manipulation of these pathways may provide a novel therapeutic approach for the treatment of allergic diseases.
Toll‐like receptor ligand treatment may have the potential to modulate allergic disorders, but the exact mechanisms of action and optimal dosage and duration of therapy are yet to be determined.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TLR ligands are potent inducers of regulatory cytokines and regulatory T cells, and are able to suppress allergic responses in vivo.
TLR agonists are potent inducers of anti‐inflammatory and tolerogenic pathways in the immune system.

TLR ligands can be used as adjuvants to enhance vaccine efficacy, and that TLR ligand administration can be beneficial for the treatment of allergic disorders by modulating the balance between pro‐ and anti‐inflammatory responses.
